COMETBOARDS is a general-purpose optimization tool developed at NASA Lewis Research Center for multidisciplinary design applications in aerospace industries.
COMETBOARDS can optimize a system defined through up to ten different disciplines, with a maximum of five subproblems per discipline.

The modular organization of COMETBOARDS includes several analyzers, such as RPK/NASTRAN for structural analysis, NEPP for air-breathing engine performance analysis, and FLOPS for aircraft performance analysis.
COMETBOARDS employs a cascade optimization strategy, using multiple state-of-the-art optimization algorithms, to solve complex multidisciplinary design problems.
In the design optimization of the support system for the International Space Station, the substructure optimization strategy in COMETBOARDS led to an optimum weight of 34.71 lb.
COMETBOARDS successfully solved five different supersonic aircraft design test cases, with the average optimum takeoff gross weight being about 1% lighter than the results from other optimizers.
For the design optimization of a mixed flow turbofan engine for a high-speed civil transport system, COMETBOARDS' cascade strategy was essential in solving the 122-mission-point problem.
COMETBOARDS is written in Fortran 77 and has been tested on Cray, Convex, SGI, and Sun Unix platforms.

The unique features of COMETBOARDS, such as design variable formulation, constraint formulation, global scaling technique, and analysis approximations, help improve convergence and reduce CPU time for solving difficult optimization problems.
COMETBOARDS has been successfully used to solve a variety of problems, including structural design, aircraft design, and air-breathing propulsion engine design.
The modular organization of COMETBOARDS allows for quick integration of new analyzers and optimizers, making it a versatile design tool for the aerospace industry.

The substructure optimization strategy in COMETBOARDS, with adequate design variable coupling and separation of local and global constraints, is an important feature for the successful optimization of large structural systems.

COMETBOARDS' cascade optimization strategy, which utilizes multiple optimizers with varying convergence criteria and analysis approximations, was crucial in solving the mixed flow turbofan engine design problem with a large number of mission points and diverse constraints.
The robustness and versatility of COMETBOARDS have been corroborated by its successful application to a number of diverse industrial problems from different disciplines in the aerospace industry.
With further enhancements and modifications, the research-level COMETBOARDS has the potential to become a useful design tool for the aerospace industry.
